transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording + transcript)
Shared artifacts: folder: https://redwood.app/pilots/maven-2026 (deck + cost-model.csv), benchmark sheet link in chat

Summary:
Kickoff for a 4-week pilot to validate unit economics and latency/throughput trade-offs for Maven AI's production chat assistant. Primary goals: validate per-token cost at target QPS, evaluate batching/caching knobs, and establish go/no-go success criteria. Team agreed to a staged benchmark with hosted + dedicated runs.

Topics covered:
- Business constraints: budget cap, timeline, stakeholders
- Workload sizing: QPS, avg tokens in/out, peak windows
- Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, throughput goals, token throughput
- Cost model: per-token estimates, batching effect, cache hit assumptions
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private and network requirements
- Next steps and action items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie (AE): Alright everybody, thanks for joining, um this is the kickoff for the Maven pilot, real quick intros?
[00:06] Raj (CTO): Raj Patel here, CTO, focusing on latency and cost, thanks.
[00:10] Maya (ML Eng): Maya — model infra and evaluation, hello.
[00:13] Evan (Finance): Evan, finance, im mostly here for budget guardrails.
[00:16] Liam (SE): Liam from Redwood, I run the bench and the infra side.
[00:18] Iris (DevOps): Iris, ops, I'll handle networking and VPCs.
[00:21] Sophie: Great. Objective for today is to lock down success criteria and the workload sizing so Liam and I can put together the cost runs. We'll aim for a 4 week pilot starting mid-July, unless we hear otherwise. Does that timing look OK?
[00:32] Raj: Yes that's fine. We want quick signal within 2 weeks ideally but ok for 4 weeks total.
[00:36] Maya: Quick question — are we running our in-house tuned LLaMA variant or one of the open models you recommend?
[00:41] Sophie: Good q. For the pilot we usually do two legs: 1) Redwood hosted with the open model you prefer (quantized variant), 2) Dedicated reserved capacity run with the same model binary to compare SLO/cost. If you want to bring-in a proprietary model we can try private deploy but that'll add a week to setup for packaging and security review.
[00:58] Raj: We can start with the open quantized model. If numbers look good, we may test our tuned model after.
[01:04] Liam: Cool. Can you walk through expected traffic profile? QPS, tokens per request, peak windows?
[01:11] Maya: Avg QPS during business hours maybe 15 rps, with peaks of 60 for a 10 min window. Avg input tokens 80, avg output 120, so ~200 tokens per request on average.
[01:23] Evan: Our initial budget for the pilot is $20k total, but we want to understand per-month run-rate if this scales.
[01:30] Sophie: Ok quick back-of-envelope: if we take 200 tokens/request * 15 rps * 3600s * 8 hours/day * 22 days ~ let's do the math, that is roughly 200*15*3600*8*22.
[01:47] Liam: That's a lot of tokens; easier to compute monthly: 15 rps * 3600 * 8 * 22 ~ 9,504,000 requests for the month, times 200 tokens = about 1.9 billion tokens.
[02:02] Raj: Whoa, that seems high, is that right?
[02:05] Maya: Hmm maybe I overstated business hours — it's more like 6 hours of steady traffic, plus peaks.
[02:09] Liam: Ok adjust: 15 rps * 3600 * 6 * 22 ~ 3,564,000 requests *200 = ~712M tokens/month.
[02:22] Evan: So ballpark 700M tokens — we need to know per-token cost to see runway.
[02:27] Sophie: For hosted we typically model two per-token numbers: inference compute (what Redwood charges per token or unit) and model-specified soft costs. For quantized open models we estimate $0.000045–0.00012 per token depending on batching and cache hit rates.
[02:41] Raj: Can you explain batching effect?
[02:44] Liam: Sure — with continuous batching we group concurrent requests so amortized compute per token drops. Example, at 15 rps with good batching you might see 30–40% reduction vs single-request baseline. But batching adds headroom to tail latency.
[03:00] Maya: What's the latency trade? We need p99 under 800ms for conversational UX or it's unacceptable.
[03:07] Liam: With a dedicated pool and small batch windows we can hit p99 ~ 600–700ms for 2K token context. Hosted tends to be slightly higher, p99 ~ 700–900ms depending on peak tail. Caching KV/prefix cache can knock off 20–50% of token compute for repeated prompts.
[03:24] Iris: For our stack, we need VPC peering or private link; can Redwood host the dedicated pool in our VPC?
[03:31] Priya (SA): Yes we have Private that can be deployed in VPC; there's an onboarding checklist and we need allowlists and KMS integration. It's typically +1 week for networking and certs.
[03:42] Raj: Security docs then? SOC2, audit logs — we need to see those before private tests.
[03:47] Sophie: We'll share SOC2 report and security packet in the drive. Action item.
[03:51] Evan: Back to cost math — if we take the lower per-token $0.000045 and 712M tokens that's $32k/month, which exceeds our $20k pilot unless Redwood discounts pilot or we do shorter run or heavy caching.
[04:06] Sophie: Right — that's why the pilot is to prove batching and prefix caching. If cache hit is 30% effective on token compute and batching gives 35% further reduction, your effective per-token could be 0.000045 * (1 - 0.30) * (1 - 0.35) ~ 0.000020 or 0.00002 per token, which on 712M tokens -> ~$14k. That's within pilot band.
[04:33] Evan: Ok that math helps, but 30% cache hit is optimistic, what drives it?
[04:37] Maya: It's repeats and shared system prompts. Our use case has big overlap since users reference prior messages and templates. We can craft prompts to maximize caching.
[04:44] Liam: We'll instrument a cache-hit simulator based on your traces — that should be an action item.
[04:49] Maya: I'll send a week of traces — obfusticated — does that work?
[04:53] Sophie: Yes, please.
[04:55] Raj: On benchmarks: what metrics will you run?
[04:58] Liam: We'll run three legs: baseline single-request latency (no batching), continuous batching with different batch windows and concurrency to measure token throughput, and prefix/KV-cache enabled run. For each leg we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:16] Raj: What's the expected wall time for these runs?
[05:18] Liam: Each leg is about 2–4 hours of steady synthetic load to stabilize tail behavior; overall bench sweep per environment ~ 1 day. We'll run hosted then dedicated the following day.
[05:27] Evan: And deliverable? A spreadsheet that shows per-token cost under the different assumptions?
[05:31] Sophie: Yes we'll provide a cost model CSV with scenario rows (cache hit %, batching factor, tokens/month) and the resulting $/month. We'll also include sensitivity analysis.
[05:39] Iris: Network egress — are there unexpected egress charges we should plan for?
[05:42] Priya: If we run in your VPC, egress is internal. Hosted will route over internet and standard cloud egress may apply; we'll flag that in the model.
[05:51] Raj: Success criteria for pilot — what do we propose?
[05:53] Sophie: Proposed success: 1) Achieve effective per-token cost <= $0.00003 under representative workload with cache+batching; 2) p99 latency <= 800ms for 95% of runs; 3) No infra breakages for 1 week of soak at 2x expected QPS. If all pass, move to 90-day reserved capacity negotiation.
[06:13] Evan: For finance to greenlight, we want a clear estimate of run-rate at projected scale (3x expected) and a path to reduce cost (quantization, distillation or scheduling).
[06:23] Liam: We'll model quantization benefits and also show the delta between hosted and dedicated per-1M token. Historically dedicated reduces per-token by ~20% at steady high utilization but requires reserved commitment.
[06:34] Maya: How about model warm-start and KV cache sizing? If we need a 32GB KV cache per GPU, do you recommend more memory?
[06:42] Priya: For long contexts with many users we recommend distributed KV caches; we'll measure memory pressure in the dedicated run.
[06:48] Raj: Timeline recap?
[06:50] Sophie: Actions and timeline: by 07/02 Sophie sends cost template; by 07/03 Maven confirms pilot users and budget; 07/07 benchmark plan; pilot run week of 07/13 for 4 weeks; mid-point check on 07/27.
[07:03] Evan: On pricing — will Redwood apply pilot credits?
[07:06] Sophie: We can offer credits to offset initial runs, we will propose an amount in the cost email. Also we'll show what a 30-day committed discount would look like.
[07:15] Iris: Any firewall or IP allowlist specifics?
[07:17] Priya: We'll provide the allowlist and cert steps; for private we need a small agent install.
[07:22] Raj: Ok good. Any blockers?
[07:24] Maya: I'll need example prompts and output schema for the eval harness.
[07:27] Liam: We'll add that to the benchmark packet.
[07:30] Evan: Finance wants weekly cost burn updates during pilot.
[07:33] Sophie: We'll include weekly snapshots in the console and a slack channel for reports.
[07:36] Raj: Great. If the pilot shows per-token under $0.00003 and p99 < 800ms, we proceed.
[07:42] Sophie: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the spreadsheet and security docs.
[07:46] Raj: Thanks all.
[07:48] End meeting.

Notes on artifacts referenced:
- cost-model.csv (starter): includes rows for: tokens/month, cache_hit_pct, batching_factor, per_token_base, effective_per_token, monthly_cost, notes
- benchmark plan: synthetic harness, 3 legs, sample load profile (6h steady, 10m peaks), sample prompts file (anonymized)
- security packet: SOC2 attestation + onboarding checklist for VPC/private

Pilot acceptance checklist (informal):
- Benchmarks completed for hosted and dedicated (deliverables: bench csv, p99 plots)
- Cost model filled with real numbers and sensitivity scenarios
- Network/VPC onboarding or IP allowlist completed
- Weekly burn dashboards shared with finance
- Mid-pilot review at 2 weeks, decision criteria met = proceed to reserved capacity discussion

End of transcript
